registry: The Japan Breach Registry 2026 — The Autumn Wave of Personal-Data Breaches at Japanese Companies and Organisations, Read from a Ledger of Primary Notices
note_on_derivation: This file is the English-only edition of data/registry.json, which is the canonical registry (bilingual, Japanese and English). It contains the English fields only; Japanese values (organisation names, verbatim wording of notices) are in data/registry.json and data/registry.csv. Quotations here are translated from the Japanese notices. URLs are unchanged. Keys differ from the canonical file: org_en is 'organisation', scale_en is 'scale', and so on; 'vector' is translated.
scope:
Personal-data breaches, or possible breaches, disclosed on or after 1 September 2026 by companies, agencies, municipalities and other organisations headquartered or principally operating in Japan. Only rows whose primary notice the author opened and read are admitted.

(Added 11 October 2026)
From the second edition onward, newly admitted rows are limited to breaches, or possible breaches, caused by external unauthorised access (including third-party intrusion, unauthorised login, and unauthorised access to a contractor or a service the organisation uses). Cases without external unauthorised access — misdelivery, mis-sent email, loss, erroneous publication, or data left viewable through a configuration error — are not admitted. Whether a case qualifies is decided by whether the notice itself describes external unauthorised access. Row 013 (Benefit One, 「プログラムの条件設定不備」, a program condition misconfiguration), admitted in the first edition, does not meet this criterion but stays as a first-edition row under the append-only rule.

(Corrected 10 November 2026)
From the fifth edition, the admission criterion is that the organisation's own primary notice was reached and its text confirms the case is in scope (a breach, or possible breach, of personal data through external unauthorised access). AI agents retrieve and check the notices, recording verbatim the sentences used as evidence; the author spot-checks notices and decides rows on the boundary of the criteria. The 300 rows up to the fourth edition are rows whose notice the author opened and read.
note_on_canonicity:
This file is the canonical registry. registry.csv and the Chapter 4 table are generated from it by scripts/build_registry.py and updated in the same commit.

(Added 15 November 2026)
In the revision of the sixth edition (v6.1), each row gained English fields (data_en, dates_en, ai_mention_en, notes_en), and two files are now generated from this file: registry.csv in Japanese only and registry_en.csv in English only. Quotations in the English fields are translated from the Japanese notices; the verbatim wording is in the Japanese fields and in registry.csv. No Japanese value was changed.
The English-only registry_en.json is also generated from this file (English fields only, with English key names). Pending entries gained English fields as well (org_en, published_en, reported_scale_en, reason_en, reference_en).

rules.verification: Through the fourth edition (001–300) the author opened and read each primary notice. From the fifth edition (301–) AI agents retrieve and check the notices, recording the evidence sentences verbatim; the author spot-checks and decides boundary cases (corrected 10 November 2026).

columns_note: Scale keeps the unit used in the notice (records, persons, accounts) and is never converted to persons. Status keeps the notice's own wording (confirmed / possible / cannot be ruled out / maximum). Vector is classified only as far as the notice states it; otherwise 'unauthorised access (vector not disclosed)'. 'AI mentioned' records whether the body of the notice refers to AI on the attacker's side; 'AI' inside company or product names is not counted.

rows.organisation: Charm (Charm Honten online pet-supply store)
rows.scale: Confirmed leak "approx. 370,000 records"; possible leak "approx. 20,000 records" (total "approx. 390,000", revised from approx. 230,000 announced on 13 August). Separately, 239 accounts with confirmed unauthorised logins
rows.data: Personal data of customers and delivery recipients (items differ by customer)
rows.dates: First notice 2026-08-13. Intrusion and detection dates not stated
rows.notes: The notice published after 1 September is an update (3rd notice); the first notice of the incident was on 13 August. Admitted because it sits on the boundary of the period, which is stated in this column. (Added 16 October 2026) The 4th notice (7 October 2026, https://www.charm.co.jp/honten/info/notice/20261007.html ) announced it had confirmed that information on customers who had cancelled their membership, "approx. 25,000 records", was affected. "For most of these a leak has been confirmed; for some data where the available records are limited, it cannot be confirmed whether a leak occurred, so they are treated as possibly leaked." "For customers who had cancelled their membership, no unauthorised login by a third party has been confirmed." Vector not stated. No mention of AI on the attacker side

rows.organisation: Helpfeel (Gyazo image-capture service)
rows.scale: User data "approx. 23.62 million records" (anonymous users without e-mail approx. 18.01 million, 76%; users with e-mail approx. 5.62 million, 24%); image metadata "approx. 490 million records"; filtered image metadata "approx. 2.4 million"; metadata of deleted images "approx. 174 million" (added in the 2nd notice)
rows.status: Confirmed exfiltration (number of persons under investigation)
rows.data: Name, email address, password hash, session ID, SSO-related information, contract plan, etc. / image ID, uploading IP address, User-Agent, EXIF location information, OCR text, etc. Payment information not affected
rows.dates: Occurred 2026-09-11, detected the same night, blocked by early hours of 12 September
rows.notes: "exploited a vulnerability that existed in the image upload server" "unauthorised access that executes arbitrary commands". 2nd notice https://corp.helpfeel.com/news/news-20260925-01 . The notice itself states that the counts are not numbers of persons. (Added 26 October 2026) 3rd notice and final report (21 October 2026, https://corp.helpfeel.com/news/news-20261021 ). The counts are the same as in the 2nd notice ("approx. 23.62 million records", "approx. 490 million records", "approx. 2.4 million records", "approx. 174 million records"). Newly, "432" images (owned by "133 persons") "were found to have been viewed and obtained by a third party"; "approx. 57,000 accounts"; reports to overseas supervisory authorities in "approx. 30 countries and regions". Vector: "there was a vulnerability whereby input values from outside were interpreted as commands on the server without being properly processed" "not caused by external software components or contractors (a so-called supply-chain attack)". "Because no log exists that records the content of the transmitted communications themselves, it is not possible to directly confirm the items or number of data sent externally". Final report received 10-15. Lists "static analysis of source code using AI" as a defensive measure, but no mention of AI on the attacker side

rows.organisation: Times Mobility (Times Car car-sharing)
rows.scale: "approx. 6.6 million" accounts (2nd notice, 28 Sep); of which identity-document images leaked for "approx. 1.6 million" accounts (3rd notice, 29 Sep)
rows.data: Name, address, date of birth, phone number, email address, driving licence information, images of identity documents, password (in a non-recoverable form), linked service IDs (9 services)
rows.notes: 1st notice https://www.park24.co.jp/news/2026/09/web1.html (no counts), 3rd notice https://www.park24.co.jp/news/2026/09/20260929-1.html . Cause under investigation. (Corrected 26 October 2026) The 5th notice (23 October 2026, https://www.park24.co.jp/news/2026/10/20261023-1.html , investor PDF https://www.park24.co.jp/news/pdf/20261023_02.pdf ) announced final figures. Times Car web system (traces of external transmission) "6,628,007 records"; identity document images (traces of external transmission) "1,464,800 records"; same (accessed only) "891,602 records"; total "2,356,402 records in total". "We had announced that approx. 1.6 million identity document image records might have leaked" → "It was found that the identity document image records for which traces of external transmission were confirmed number approx. 1.46 million." Times Club web: club card numbers "19,510 records", linked service IDs "135,436 records", and others. The vector was announced for the first time: "We have determined that this incident occurred because a vulnerability that existed in the web system was exploited" "We have confirmed that, after intruding into the system by exploiting the vulnerability, the attacker searched the information in the system and used the information obtained to access the database and file areas". This row's vector classification is kept as the value at the first notice (vector not disclosed). Identity document images to be "deleted by the end of October 2026"; "cash or vouchers worth 3,000 yen"; revision of the full-year earnings forecast. No mention of AI on the attacker side

rows.notes: The author checked against the text of the timely disclosure (the same text distributed via TDnet). Vector: "we are proceeding with a detailed investigation". (Added 26 October 2026) 20 October 2026, "On future measures to strengthen security and personal information protection in the 'Yakiniku King' official app" (https://www.monogatari.co.jp/news/261020_news/ ). rows.organisation: GMO Research & AI (infoQ survey panel)
rows.scale: "up to 948,498 records" (all records held as of 5 Oct). Fraudulent point exchanges: 611 cases, ¥2,869,500
rows.status: Unauthorised access confirmed; count is a maximum
rows.data: Name, name reading (furigana), sex, date of birth, email address, address, phone number, encrypted password, member ID, points held, etc.
rows.dates: Intrusion from 2026-10-02 onward; confirmed morning of 2026-10-03; attack path blocked at 14:15 the same day
rows.notes: "intruded by exploiting a vulnerability in software used on our site". The "AI" in the company name is not a reference to the attack method. (Corrected 16 October 2026) The 2nd notice (14 October 2026, https://gmo-research.ai/pressroom/notice/notice-20261014 ) finalised the count. "In the 1st notice we announced up to 948,498 records, but as a result of subsequent investigation we have determined that the number of records of personal information taken outside is 894,082." The breakdown of the difference: "taken outside but containing no personal information" 9,068 records ("records of members for whom more than two months had passed since cancellation and whose personal information had already been deleted under our privacy statement") and "not taken outside" 45,348 records. Vector: "We have confirmed that a third party intruded by exploiting a vulnerability in software used on our site" (unchanged). "On 7 October we invalidated the passwords of all members." The unauthorised point exchanges (611 cases, 2,869,500 yen) are the same as in the 1st notice. This row's "up to 948,498 records" is kept as the value at the 1st notice. No mention of AI on the attacker side

rows.organisation: Scala Communications (i-ask FAQ system)
rows.scale: "up to 713,126" enquiry records (gross, with duplicates); "up to 5" client companies
rows.data: Inquiry information (name, email address, content of inquiry, etc.; differs by company)
rows.dates: About 20:30 on 2026-10-02 to about 8:00 on 10-03; blocked about 8:00 on 10-03
rows.notes: "logged in to the i-ask administration site without authorisation and, after installing a malicious program,". Press reports identify it as a contractor of Daiwa Securities, but this notice does not name Daiwa Securities (Corrected 21 November 2026) 2nd notice (https://scala-com.jp/news/2026/11-1/ , title "Apology and notice regarding personal information leakage due to unauthorised access to the FAQ system 'i-ask' (2nd notice)", 2026.11.13). Count: "Affected are 4 client companies*, 552,179 records (cumulative)." "*We previously reported up to 5 companies, but as a result of the investigation we confirmed that information of 1 of them was not taken outside." (changed from this row's "up to 713,126 records" and "up to 5 companies"). Route: "At 20:32 on 2 October 2026, login attempts to the administration site began from an external IP address, and at 20:34 the attacker succeeded in logging in." "At 20:36, a malicious program (WebShell) was installed by abusing the image upload function." Cause: "Changing the initial password of i-ask accounts (including administrators) and restricting access sources to the administration site were optional settings for each client company, and the service could be used without them." "As a result, unauthorised login occurred from one company that had been operating with the initial password issued by us." "The setting prohibiting uploaded files from being executed as programs was insufficient." Status: "We have confirmed that compressed files containing information were taken outside by the attacker, and have judged that the information was stolen." "As of today, no secondary damage such as misuse of personal information resulting from this incident has been confirmed." The vector classification (unauthorised login) does not change (initial password and insufficient settings are described as causes). No mention of AI on the attacker side (the word AI appears only in the preventive measure "4. Introduction of AI-based anomaly detection and expansion of monitoring scope (implemented)") (2026-11-13, https://scala-com.jp/news/2026/11-1/ )

rows.organisation: IDC Frontier (IDCF Cloud)
rows.scale: "495 companies and municipalities" contracting IDCF Cloud (number of contracting organisations, not of personal records)
rows.status: Exfiltration of personal data not stated
rows.data: Customer companies' data
rows.dates: Occurred from about 3:40 on 2026-10-07 and continuing
rows.notes: "it was found to be caused by a ransomware attack by a third party". This row is not itself an announcement of a personal-data leak, but it is admitted because it is the origin of the vector for row 027 (JR East). (Corrected 16 October 2026) 5th notice (14 October 2026, https://www.idcf.jp/news/topics/20261014001 ). "From these facts, we have determined that there was no outflow of data to the outside." "Of the 495 companies and local governments affected by the outage, we have confirmed that backup data can be retrieved for the 194 customers who were using the 'snapshot function' of IDCF Cloud." Newly, "We have confirmed that unauthorised queries were made against the registered information of 48 customer companies in the 'IDCF Cloud Portal'" "The information queried without authorisation includes email addresses that may contain the personal names of contact persons at 2 companies (1 record each)." The intrusion vector is listed as an item under investigation, but the result is not stated. The 3rd notice (8 October, https://www.idcf.jp/news/topics/20261008001 ) says "unauthorised access by a third party (ransomware attack)"; the 4th notice (9 October, https://www.idcf.jp/news/topics/20261009001 ) reports on the response structure. No mention of AI on the attacker side. (Added 26 October 2026) The 6th notice (18 October 2026, https://www.idcf.jp/news/topics/20261018001 ) concerns the resumption of the backup service. "The 'snapshot function' *2 is still suspended to confirm its safety." Intrusion vector and counts not stated. The downstream cases View Card (042) and JR Kyushu (043) were admitted on 26 October (Corrected 3 November 2026) The 7th notice (27 October 2026, https://www.idcf.jp/news/topics/20261027001 ) announced the investigation results. The vector was found: "The unauthorised access by a third party occurred because a vulnerability in open-source software adopted in the 'IDCF Cloud Portal' was exploited." "It was found that a third party had intruded into the authentication system by exploiting a vulnerability in the open-source software used in the authentication system of the 'IDCF Cloud Portal'." Changed from the 5th notice's "48 companies" and "2 companies (1 record each)" to "We have confirmed that unauthorised queries were made against the registered information of up to 71 customer companies." "The information queried without authorisation includes personal names and email addresses that may contain personal names, etc., for up to 31 companies (31 records)." Login passwords "were confirmed to have been changed without authorisation, up to 4 cases." "There was no outflow to the outside of data within customers' virtual servers." "We have not contacted the attacker and have not paid or negotiated any ransom." Start date of the intrusion not stated. This row's vector classification is kept as the value at the first notice (vector not disclosed). The notice states "We will also work to further strengthen security measures and governance to respond to cyber attacks that are becoming more sophisticated and ingenious as AI evolves." (a reference to attacks in general; it does not say AI was used in this attack. Whether to count it in ai_mention is the author's decision)

rows.dates: (1) Occurred 2026-10-02 to 04, discovered 10-05; (2) occurred 09-20, discovered 09-28; (3) 2026-08-03 to 10-01, discovered 10-01
rows.notes: (1) "some administrative functions were operated without authorisation", (2) "a vulnerability in the business management system was exploited", (3) "the booking completion page could be displayed without logging in" (misconfiguration). One notice contains three vectors. (Added 16 October 2026) Notice on the parent company's site of the opening of a telephone helpline (13 October 2026, https://jp.adventurekk.com/news/data-leak-call-center-notice/ ). No change to counts or vectors. (Corrected 26 October 2026) 2nd notice (16 October 2026, https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67630 ). "It was found that credit card information, etc. of some customers who used 'skyticket Premium' has flowed out" "Number of persons: up to 6,140" "Items: credit card number, cardholder name, expiry date (for some customers, card number only)" "*Security codes are not included." "The card information was encrypted, but because the information used for the encryption was also obtained without authorisation, the card information may be read". "Until June 2018, card information was stored on our servers" "Records (logs) relating to payment of membership fees remained on our servers without being deleted" "We confirmed that this log was obtained on 3 October through the unauthorised access between 2 and 4 October 2026". The 1st notice's statements such as "passport numbers not leaked" stand, but its statement on card numbers was corrected. No mention of AI on the attacker side (Corrected 3 November 2026) 3rd notice (30 October 2026, https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67691 ). "Subsequent investigation found that part of the payment-related data we stored was read without authorisation and that bank account information for refunds flowed out" "and that part of the credit card information and information relating to travel insurance applications may have flowed out." Bank account information for refunds "Count: 32,341 records"; part of the credit card information "Count: approx. 936,000 records (approx. 414,000 persons)" ("cardholder name, partly masked card number (last 4 digits only, or first 6 and last 4 digits), browser information"; "the full card number, expiry date and security code are not included"); information relating to travel insurance applications "Count: approx. 118,000 records (approx. 119,000 persons)". Status: "We confirmed that, of the data read, the part containing bank account information for refunds was sent to the outside." "For the other parts, no traces of external transmission have been confirmed, but because the possibility of transmission cannot be ruled out, we are announcing them as possibly having flowed out." Vector: "We had kept copies (backups) of databases obtained in the past on the cloud without deleting them even after they were no longer needed." "In the unauthorised access between 2 and 4 October 2026 announced in the 1st notice, authentication information obtained without authorisation was misused and part of these copies was read." Correction of the 2nd notice: "The information that flowed out stated in the 2nd notice was the member ID and name set internally by us for the use of 'skyticket Premium'," "and we have confirmed that it was not the member ID, name and password of Benefit Station, so we correct it." This row's vector classification (multiple vectors) is not changed. No mention of AI on the attacker side (Corrected 21 November 2026) 4th notice (https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67764 , title "Apology and notice regarding the outflow of customer information due to unauthorised access (4th notice)", 18 November 2026, "(Updated 19 November 2026: corrected the passport-related text in '4. Requests to customers')"). "In connection with the unauthorised access announced in 'Apology and notice regarding the outflow of customer information due to unauthorised access' of 9 October 2026 (the '1st notice'), the 2nd notice of the 16th of that month and the 3rd notice of the 28th of that month," "subsequent investigation found that some functions of skyticket's payment server were misused by a third party and reservation information (including passport information of some customers) flowed out." Affected: "customers (including companions) who completed application and payment on skyticket between approx. 07:01 and 12:18 on 20 September 2026." Count: "1,045 reservations, approx. 1,166 persons (857 applicants, approx. 309 companions)"; "passport information (15 persons among international air ticket reservations): passport number, expiry date, issuing country, nationality". Route: "On skyticket's payment server, a connection-permission setting for a function used for inter-system integration, which was to have been deleted in 2024, remained, so the function could be used from outside." "On 20 September 2026 a third party misused this function and obtained the above reservation information." Discovery: "In the course of investigating misuse of the same function on 22 October of the same year (reservation information of 16 persons; affected customers have been contacted individually), we traced back the access records and became aware of this matter on 12 November." Blocking: "On 28 October 2026 we blocked external access to the function." On the 1st notice: "In the 1st notice we announced that, regarding the unauthorised access to our servers, 'we have confirmed that passport numbers have not flowed out'." (a result different from 'no passport numbers leaked' in this row's data_ja). Companions' names "may be read, because the information used for encryption was also obtained through the unauthorised access announced in the 1st notice." Note: the 4th notice dates the 3rd notice 'the 28th of that month', whereas the notes record the 3rd notice (https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67691 ) as dated 30 October 2026 (the list also shows the 3rd notice as 2026/10/30). The route for this event is a leftover setting (misconfiguration), within this row's vector classification (composite). No mention of AI on the attacker side. Separately, 13 November 2026 "Notice on the end of the dedicated telephone line for the unauthorised access and transition to email support" (https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67753 , body not read) (2026-11-18, https://skyticket.jp/news/maintenance/67764 )

rows.scale: Estimated "approx. 9 million records (cumulative) including email addresses were output"; "5 systems in total"
rows.data: "Information including email addresses"
rows.dates: Detected early hours of 2026-10-16
rows.notes: Timely disclosure (original https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/4372/tdnet/2896738/00.pdf ; what the author could reach was the same text distributed by Yahoo! Finance). It confirmed "that, through a program vulnerability, authentication information of our support and quality-control staff for the services was obtained". Downstream announcements by client organisations exist (row 058 Nomura Securities, Saitama Prefecture and others). The count is a cumulative count, not a number of persons (Corrected 3 November 2026) 2nd notice (26 October 2026, https://www.ymir.co.jp/info/ymir-information20261027.html , title "Report on unauthorised access to our systems (2nd notice)"). "We have confirmed that the systems in which output of email addresses, etc. was confirmed as a result of the unauthorised access total 49 systems."; cumulative count "51,628,280 records (cumulative count)". "There are currently 16 systems for which the number of leaked records is under investigation, and the cumulative count may increase with further investigation." In the customer management portal "Cuenote BASE", "our services' subscriber information was in a viewable state" ("190 records"; company name, name, phone, email address). Added to the vector: "V. referring to data in other systems via a malicious program" "VI. We have confirmed that session information at system login was obtained and used for unauthorised login". "At present, no fact that the leaked personal information has been published to an unspecified number of people, and no misuse of personal information resulting from this incident, has been confirmed." The 1st notice's "cumulative approx. 9 million records" and "5 systems in total" are kept as this row's values. The company's timely-disclosure PDF (https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/4372/tdnet/2898564/00.pdf , as cited in press reports) was not read by the author. No mention of AI on the attacker side (Corrected 14 November 2026) 3rd notice of 11 November 2026 (https://www.ymir.co.jp/info/ymir-information20261111.html , title "Report on unauthorised access to our systems (3rd notice)"). The Cuenote FC count became "delivery-destination information: cumulative 47,864,147 records" ("(attribute information such as email addresses and names)"), down from the 2nd notice's cumulative count ("51,628,280 records (cumulative count)" in this row's notes). The reason: "Through subsequent log matching and database analysis, we strictly identified and excluded the records actually output, excluded records that had been counted twice, etc.," (the second half of the sentence not verified verbatim). Affected: "49 systems (part of dedicated ASPs)"; Cuenote BASE "190 records". The statement of the vector became more specific: "A method of exploiting a program vulnerability to use a malicious program inside the server to intrude directly into the database at the core of the system and output data." "A method of exploiting a program vulnerability to steal the temporary session information of legitimate users who were logged in at the time and enter the administration screen by impersonating legitimate users." The timeline includes "began deleting, from all platforms, the common maintenance and QA accounts that caused the lateral movement" (2026/10/18 13:00). "Details of the data items that flowed out are still being confirmed and will be announced as soon as they are known." "No outflow of payment information such as credit card information has been confirmed at present." On the final report: "When we receive the investigation report from that body, we plan to publish a 'final report' as a summary of the investigation results." The vector classification (vulnerability) does not change. The 1st notice's "cumulative approx. 9 million records" and "5 systems in total" are kept as this row's values. No mention of AI on the attacker side (the word AI appears only in the company's preventive measures, "source code review using AI"; not verified verbatim). Note: on the same page, a statement giving output via session abuse as "42 systems" coexists with the table's "49 systems" (pointed out by WebFetch; not verified verbatim) (Added 21 November 2026) The full sentence on the count in the 3rd notice (https://www.ymir.co.jp/info/ymir-information20261111.html ) is: "Through subsequent log matching and database analysis, we strictly identified and excluded the records actually output, excluded records that had been counted twice, etc., and confirmed that the delivery-destination information is 'cumulative approx. 47.86 million records (47,864,147 records)'." On the note that '42 systems' coexists with '49 systems' in the table: '42 systems' appears in the timeline (2026/10/25 21:45) as "Through analysis of all logs, newly identified data output via session abuse (42 systems)"; the damage-summary table reads "Program vulnerabilities etc. were exploited and information leakage occurred in 49 systems (part of dedicated ASPs)"; and a heading reads "- 2nd notice (45 systems newly added, 49 systems in total)". 42 can be read as the number of systems in which output via session abuse was identified, and 49 as the total (author's judgement). The company's notices list (https://www.ymir.co.jp/info/ , as retrieved 21 November 2026) has no 4th or final notice, and no follow-up between 2026-11-14 and 11-20 (2026-11-11, https://www.ymir.co.jp/info/ymir-information20261111.html )

rows.scale: "Total number of records leaked or possibly leaked: 22,527" (19th report, 2026-11-03); the 6th report said up to 30 addresses per mail magazine possibly viewed
rows.status: Email addresses possibly viewed; no direct exfiltration of personal data found
rows.data: Email addresses of recipients managed in clients' delivery environments. Data that may have been taken out or read from the portal site (setup scripts, connection information with payment agencies, configuration files, etc.): "We have confirmed that it does not include personal information of customers or other individuals." (7th notice). The connection information "does not include credit card information, etc." (not verified verbatim)
rows.dates: Maintenance began (portal blocked) about 3:50 on 2026-10-24; suspicious communications confirmed and some delivery environments stopped 10:45 on 10-24 (2nd notice); administrator login information for all delivery environments updated about 11:44 on 10-24; traces of unauthorised intrusion confirmed 18:08 on 10-24 (5th notice); first report to Hachioji Police Station and relevant ministries 10-24; police reference number and IPA receipt number published 10-28; the Personal Information Protection Commission instructed a joint report with clients 10-28 (dates are the times of each notice's additions; not verified verbatim)
rows.notes: "Because traces of aggressive access and unauthorised intrusion by an outside third party have now been confirmed, we have put the portal site into maintenance." "Using authentication information that may have leaked in the attack, the web applications of some customers' delivery environments were intruded into, and phishing emails may have been sent to recipients managed by customers there." The 7th notice gives the trigger for the intrusion as "setup scripts for customer environments" (not verified verbatim). Classified as "multiple vectors" as a two-stage intrusion: into the portal, then into delivery environments using authentication information obtained there (author's decision). A single page with the 2nd to 18th notices (2026-11-01 15:32) added in turn; there is no notice explicitly labelled "1st notice" on the page. The 17th notice (10-31) says existing customers' delivery environments are expected to resume in turn from around 4 November (not verified verbatim). The only personal-information relevance is the possibility that email addresses were viewed; removal has not been confirmed. Admission is the author's decision. Notices by client organisations (according to press reports, Futaba Town, Minamiuonuma City and others) have not been checked; each is a candidate for a separate row (3 November 2026, primary notice re-retrieved and checked) The 19th notice (2026-11-03) is on the same page and reports a total of 22,527 records. rows.organisation: Arara (email delivery service "Arara Message")
rows.data: "Email addresses held by user companies using this environment"
rows.dates: Unauthorised access occurred and confirmed Wednesday 2026-10-28; the server disconnected from the network (no date)
rows.notes: "In some environments of our system, a vulnerability in a web server was exploited by a third party." "We have confirmed unauthorised access to one system among the server systems of the email delivery service we provide, and that approx. 3.01 million email addresses held by user companies using this environment were taken outside." The candidate announcement date was 10/28, but the pages of 10/28 (https://am.arara.com/news/2026102801 , /2026102802) say only "The service has been stopped due to the effects of unauthorised access", with no statement of a leak. The leak first appears in the notice dated 10/29, so published=2026-10-29. The 2nd notice in press reports (11/2, approx. 77 million records) was not in the arara.com notice list (at the time of retrieval). In res_1029_1102.json it is excluded as "outside the range (10/28)", but since the leak was announced on 10/29 it is appropriate to treat it as a row within that range (beware of duplication). The contractor for the rows of the four Paydon banks, the Japan Society of Civil Engineers, Okinawa Prefecture, Suzuki and AUTHENTIC JAPAN. Another article in the notice list mentions "Email × AI × Sales" (the company's own seminar name), outside the text. The 2nd notice (2 November 2026, https://www.arara.com/dcms_media/other/arara_20261102__.pdf ) was not read by the author. Another investigation's record gives "approx. 77 million records" and user companies intruded into "up to approx. 380 companies" (not verified verbatim). The first notice's "approx. 3.01 million records" was re-retrieved on 2026-11-03 and the wording verified ("We have confirmed that approx. 3.01 million email addresses held by user companies using this environment were taken outside."; vector "a vulnerability in a web server was exploited by a third party.") (Corrected 8 November 2026) 3rd notice of 6 November 2026 (https://www.arara.com/news/info/20261106_arara ): "The email addresses taken out number 81,329,467 (approx. 81 million), excluding duplicates" (the count after removing duplicates between the categories of unauthorised access via this service, 78,102,937; the shared environment, 2,842,400; and another cloud environment, 3,249,492; the shared-environment count was revised from the 2nd notice's 3,386,187). "We estimate the affected client companies at up to approx. 380 companies (under examination)". "From 28 to 30 October, up to approx. 7.13 million suspicious emails impersonating credit card companies were sent from the sender 'news@arara.com'." All services were stopped on 31 October. On the intrusion path: "we are proceeding with identification". (Added 21 November 2026) The Arara Message temporary site (https://am.arara.com/info/news/ ) carries "Correction of, and apology for, the content of individual notifications concerning unauthorised access to 'Arara Message' (6 November 2026)". "On 2 November we individually notified some business partners subject to '2.(1) Unauthorised access via this service' in the 2nd notice of the details of this incident." "At that time we conveyed incorrect information about the period during which data was taken out, so we correct it as follows." Wrong: "Data was taken out of each server at some point between 28 and 29 October." -> Correct: "From 28 October until the service was stopped on 31 October, data was continuously taken out of each server (the date and time of exfiltration differs by server)." "In addition, with the correction of the exfiltration period, the scope of data subject to the outflow (scope of impact) conveyed individually to some business partners was also wrong." The correction concerns individual notifications to client companies; this row's values ("approx. 3.01 million email addresses", vector: vulnerability) do not change. The item has no separate URL; it is posted in the notices section of the temporary site (2026-11-06, https://am.arara.com/info/news/ ) (Added 21 November 2026) Arara Message temporary site (https://am.arara.com/info/news/ , "Last updated: 19 November 2026 23:00"). "The application deadline for joint reports and proxy reports to the Personal Information Protection Commission closed at 23:00 on Thursday 19 November 2026." On the timing of service resumption: "It remains undecided at present." "We are individually informing customers of the impact on each customer (whether information flowed out, the number of records, details) in turn, starting with customers whose investigation results have been finalised." "We are continuing to investigate the scope of impact." No update to counts or vector (procedural update). On the arara.com notices list (https://www.arara.com/news/info/ ), the 6 November article is the latest; there is no 4th notice or later (as retrieved 21 November 2026) (2026-11-19, https://am.arara.com/info/news/ )

The count was revised from the first notice's "up to approx. 350,000 records" to "Across RGα as a whole, the member information of 320,720 records may have leaked." (breakdown "- facilities in use: 93 facilities / 187,687 records" "- cancelled facilities: 82 facilities / 133,033 records"). The status words are "possibility" and "risk". The data affected increased: "In addition to the six items announced in the first notice, it was found that the following information may also have leaked." ("7. name in kana" "8. mobile phone number" "9. fax number" "10. date of birth" "11. sex" "12. employer information (company name, department, postal code, address, phone number, fax number)"). The vector is "was subjected to unauthorised access by a third party exploiting a vulnerability", and the classification (vulnerability) does not change. As secondary harm, "We have confirmed that phishing emails (fake emails) apparently misusing the leaked information are being sent to customers who made accommodation bookings after registering as members." (the text lures recipients to "download a dedicated authentication app"). No mention of AI on the attacker side. The first notice's "up to approx. 350,000 records" is kept as this row's value

The page of 11/4 (https://www.e-design.net/company/information/2026/2026_11_04.html ) only announces the suspension of procedures due to "emergency system maintenance", with no statement of unauthorised access (10 November 2026, primary notice re-retrieved and checked: the notice says "the service used as the path of the unauthorised access", but does not give the service name or contractual relationship. The 74 records are "the number of records of personal information that may have leaked that we have grasped at present") (Corrected 14 November 2026) The notice at the same URL became "(updated 9 November 2026)", and the count under the heading "2. Personal information that leaked (as of 9 November 2026)" was revised to "71 records (the number of persons whose leak has been confirmed at present, including related persons, is 93)". This row's "74 records" (records that may have leaked) does not appear on the page, and the word "possibility" does not appear near the count ("leak has been confirmed"). The data affected lists "accident-related information: accident date and time, place, details, claim amount paid, name of the other party, etc.", "Tokio Marine Direct app information: driving trip information obtained during the contract period", "credit card information: credit card company name, last 4 digits of the credit card number only, expiry date" and others (the difference from the 11/5 version not verified verbatim). "74 records" is kept as this row's value. The re-check of 10 November 2026 in the existing notes (74 records) differs from the version of the page retrieved today (updated 9 November, 71 records). rows.notes: Title ("On the temporary suspension of the Takarakuji official website and official app", 6 November 2026). Issued in the name of "all prefectures and all designated cities"; the contact is the Takarakuji call centre. Wording of the status: "As a result of the investigation, we confirmed that on the Takarakuji official website there were unauthorised logins by a third party for some customers, and that, in addition to customers' passwords being changed unintentionally, member information may have been viewed by that third party." "At present, there are no traces of intrusion into the servers or databases of the Takarakuji official website, and no outflow of member data has been confirmed." Wording of the vector: "there may have been unauthorised logins using a list of email addresses and passwords obtained elsewhere". The PDF is on takarakuji-preliminary.jp, linked from https://sorry.takarakuji-official.jp/Sorry-PlannedMaintenance.html (a notice page to which www.takarakuji-official.jp redirects with 302). The percent-encoded URL was rejected by the WebFetch proxy because of its length, so it was retrieved with the URL in Japanese. The 9 November PDF "On ways to buy Takarakuji other than the official website" has no new statement on unauthorised logins or counts. (10 November 2026, primary notice re-retrieved and checked: the notice says "we confirmed that member information may have been viewed by that third party." "No outflow of member data has been confirmed either." On the boundary of admission criterion 2) (Added 14 November 2026) In the update of 11 November 2026, it announced the items of member information that may have been viewed: "name, date of birth, sex, address, phone number, email address, prize-receiving account information (financial institution name, first 4 digits of the account number, account holder), credit card information (last 4 digits of the credit card number), purchase history (lottery type, amount, win/loss information), profile image (registrants only)". "At present, there are no traces of intrusion into the servers or databases of the Takarakuji official website, and no outflow of member data has been confirmed." "Because this matter may be unauthorised logins using email addresses and passwords obtained elsewhere (a so-called 'list-based attack')". No count stated. Title "On the temporary suspension of the Takarakuji official website and official app" (11 November 2026 (updated)). Primary URL: https://www.takarakuji-preliminary.jp/newsrelease_20261111.pdf

rows.dates: "At about 18:30 on Thursday 5 November 2026, we confirmed that unauthorised access from outside had been carried out against the server hosting the EC site we operate and that part of customers' personal information may have leaked."
rows.notes: Title "Apology and notice regarding the possibility of a personal information leak due to unauthorised access to our EC site" (6 November 2026). Vector: "It was found that unauthorised access from outside exploiting a system vulnerability was carried out against part of the server area storing 'log files' that temporarily record the operating status and communication processing of our EC site." The list of data items not verified verbatim (WebFetch's excerpt). (Added 14 November 2026) Timely disclosure of 10 November 2026 (title "On the personal information leak following unauthorised access to our EC site and the suspension of services"). It gives the start of the emergency stop as "From 22:00 on Saturday 7 November, we emergency-stopped the various related services." Counts: "(up to 13,685 persons)", "EDION gift card information (5,360 cards)", "(up to 1,141 persons)"; card information "(order error logs: up to 5 records)", "up to 556 times". Cause: "a malicious program had been embedded in the payment information input processing for the PC environment". The timely-disclosure original https://www.release.tdnet.info/inbs/140120261110571388.pdf is blocked by robots, so it was checked against the same text distributed by Yahoo! Finance. Primary URL: https://finance-frontend-pc-dist.west.edge.storage-yahoo.jp/disclosure/20261110/20261110571388.pdf (Corrected 14 November 2026) 2nd notice of 9 November 2026 (https://www.edion.co.jp/system/files/news-release/pdf/ja/2026-11/20261109_pr_1_1.pdf , title "Apology and notice regarding a newly found incident on our EC site, the possibility of a personal information leak and the suspension of services (2nd notice)"). New incident: "It was newly found that the payment-related processing within our EC site had been tampered with by an outside third party who embedded a malicious program." (the malicious program began running "shortly after 19:00 on Wednesday 4 November"; affected are new card entries on PCs, "Number affected: up to 556 times (when card information was newly entered on the payment information input screen)"). It revised the 1st notice's statement: "Also, while we reported that the investigation at the time of the 1st notice had not confirmed a leak of credit card information or login passwords, subsequent detailed analysis newly found that some such information was included." ("credit card information (order error logs: up to 5 records)", "login IDs and login passwords (up to 1,141 persons)"). "EDION gift cards confirmed to have leaked (5,360 cards)". Service suspension: "From 22:00 on Saturday 7 November, we took the precautionary measure of emergency-stopping various services including our EC site." (reopening of the EC site undecided). The vector classification (vulnerability) is kept as the value at the 1st notice (the 2nd notice does not state the intrusion path for the tampering). No mention of AI on the attacker side. The 1st notice's "up to 4,131 persons" and "up to 9,554 persons" are kept as this row's values

rows.dates: "On Monday 19 October 2026, unauthorised access occurred to the system used by Benefit One's contractor." "Then, on Wednesday 28 October, we received a report from Benefit One that the personal information of 2,622 customers had leaked." "Further, on Thursday 5 November, we received an additional report that approx. 190,000 items of administrative identification information we use to identify customers had also leaked to the outside."
rows.notes: Title: "Notice and apology regarding the personal information leak in 'Eraberu Gold Yutai' provided by Benefit One Inc." (9 November 2026). Wording of the vector: "the system used by Benefit One's contractor was subjected to unauthorised access by a third party". The notice's wording is a service "provided by Benefit One", and Benefit One is a partner (classified as contractor). The contractor's name is not stated. The service has been "temporarily suspended" since 22 October 2026. Because the affected service ("Eraberu Gold Yutai") and the date of occurrence (19 October) differ, it was treated as a separate case from existing row 207 (Benefit One "Tokugai", contractor Forestec, occurred 14 October 2026) and from Credit Saison's "Tokugai" notice of the same period (https://www.saisoncard.co.jp/customer-support/information/20261028/ , 29,465 persons). However, the text does not name the contractor, so whether it is the same contractor as Forestec (the same chain) is not confirmed. Benefit One's own announcement on "Eraberu Gold Yutai" could not be found in its notice list (October–November 2026) (only "Tokugai" of 10/28). Also a separate case from existing rows 281 (real-estate ST) and 364 (MUJI Card).

rows.organisation: Osaka Metropolitan University (university IT infrastructure; terminal of NEC's subcontractor and NEC-managed cloud storage)
rows.scale: approx. 170,000 persons' personal data (students and staff), of which approx. 1,400 persons' highly sensitive data (from NEC-managed cloud storage etc.); separately approx. 130,000 records in the university's own academic systems flagged as possibly leaked
rows.status: Confirmed leak from NEC/subcontractor side; possible leak from the university's own systems
rows.data: "Personal information such as students' and staff's IDs, names, email addresses and dates of birth" "highly confidential personal information such as bank account numbers, health-related information, passport images and passport numbers", and also "information important for the university's administration (including administrator information for the university's information systems)"
rows.dates: 1st notice: a large-scale outage "in the early hours of Friday 2 October 2026". 3rd notice (2026-10-06): "We have determined that this incident was caused by a cyber attack, a so-called ransomware attack, and". 5th notice (2026-10-21): "a company to which NEC subcontracts system development and maintenance (hereinafter 'the subcontractor') was subjected to a cyber attack in late September 2026" "We received a report that the cause was unauthorised access to the university's systems using a legitimate account held by the subcontractor."
rows.notes: Title "On the occurrence of an outage in the university's information infrastructure system [6th notice]" (2026-11-13). The first notice is "On the occurrence of an outage in the university's information infrastructure system [1st notice]" (2026-10-02, https://www.omu.ac.jp/news/4875). However, the 1st and 2nd notices (same day, https://www.omu.ac.jp/news/4876) say "We have not yet identified the cause at present." and contain no statement of an external attack or personal information. An external attack first appears in the 3rd notice (2026-10-06, https://www.omu.ac.jp/news/4873; determined to be ransomware; "whether personal information flowed out is currently under investigation"), and confirmation of a leak first appears in the 5th notice (2026-10-21, https://www.omu.ac.jp/news/4877; "We are confirming with NEC details such as the content and number of the leaked information."). published was set to the first notice's 10/02 (as instructed), but the "announcement of a leak (or possibility)" for admission criterion 1 is satisfied on 10/06 or 10/21, and the handling of the announcement date needs a decision at merging. The 4th notice https://www.omu.ac.jp/news/4856 not read. The 6th notice's attachment PDF https://www.omu.ac.jp/_media/pressrelease20261113_bessi1-original.pdf not read. Change in scale: 5th notice "details being confirmed with NEC" → 6th notice "approx. 170,000 persons" and "approx. 1,400 persons". Wording of the vector in the 6th notice: "There was a report that a terminal of the company that is NEC's subcontractor (hereinafter 'the subcontractor') was subjected to unauthorised access." Possibly the same NEC chain as existing rows 057 (NEC, via a contractor, 2026-10-20) and 058 (Osaka University, contractor NEC, 2026-10-21), but whether the notices explicitly state it is the same incident has not been confirmed. The omu.moe domain that an aggregator site gives as the first notice's URL is not the university's official domain and was not used.

rows.dates: Unauthorised access: around 11 October to around 13 October 2026 (suspicious behaviour confirmed at 16:30 on 11 October; not verified verbatim). Unauthorised email delivery: 1:17 to 7:16 on 13 October (17th notice); via API 22 to 23 October (25th notice). 1st notice "[1st notice] updated 15:50, 13 October". 26th notice: updated 6 November 2026
rows.notes: Title "On the series of responses following unauthorised access to our services" (SpeeCAN RAIDEN official blog, published 2026/10/13, updated as needed). Linked from the notice on the company's own site https://www.arcadia.co.jp/info/4076 ("(2026/11/06)"); the contact section at the end of the article names "Arcadia Co., Ltd." and the text says "SpeeCAN RAIDEN operated by the company", so it was judged to be a notice on the domain of the organisation's service (author's decision). The sentence used for the judgement (2nd notice): "We confirmed that unauthorised access by a third party was carried out on SpeeCAN RAIDEN, which we operate, and that personal information may have leaked." The initial intrusion path is stated only as "The intrusion path from outside has been identified" (not verified verbatim), with no statement of the method. 25th notice (the cause of subsequent unauthorised email sending): "1) during the unauthorised access from 11 to 13 October, the account for the email sending API leaked," "the password was cracked by brute force, and the email sending API was used without authorisation from outside" "a URL parse confusion vulnerability was exploited," (each part of a sentence). Affected domains (14th notice): raiden.ktaiwork.jp, raiden2.ktaiwork.jp, raiden3.ktaiwork.jp, raiden2.speecan.jp, s.ktaiwork.jp, s2.ktaiwork.jp, NET119 (net119.speecan.jp, net119fd.speecan.jp), 119RAIDEN (fs119.ktaiwork.jp). ai_mention: "RAIDEN" is a product name and is not counted. The parent case of client organisations' existing rows 303 (Okazaki City), 305 (Yanai City) and 309 (Funabashi City). Pending Fukuoka City (10/14) is presumed to be in the same chain (not confirmed). Moved from pending (14 November 2026). (Re-check of 14 November 2026) The scale field is the 2nd notice's value; counts for other services were added in the 4th and 11th notices. The two paths in the 25th notice (brute-forcing the password of the API sending account; URL parse confusion vulnerability) are written as the causes of the unauthorised email delivery of 22–23 October, not as the path of the personal-information leak, so the vector remains vector not disclosed. (Corrected 21 November 2026) At the same URL (https://raiden.site.ktaiwork.jp/archives/4597 ) there are the 26th notice (06 November 16:15, "We have resumed the 'suspension of API integration from external systems' announced in [19th notice].") and the 27th notice (19 November 13:15, "We report preliminary results of the vulnerability assessment and dark-web investigation by external bodies." "Details will be reported in the final report." "The final report is scheduled to be prepared around early December."). The 27th notice's attachment "Vulnerability assessment results report (preliminary)" (dated 19 November 2026) states "It was confirmed that the 'directory path traversal vulnerability', which was the direct cause of this unauthorised access, has been resolved." and "No significant vulnerability with a major impact on the security of all cloud services we provide was confirmed." The attachment "Dark-web investigation results on personal information that may have leaked (preliminary)" (same date) states "No fact was confirmed that personal information that may have leaked from our systems has been published on the internet." Because the direct cause of the initial intrusion (a directory path traversal vulnerability) is stated in a primary document for the first time, this row's vector 'Unauthorised access (route not disclosed)' corresponds to 'Vulnerability' (the original value is not changed; to be decided at merge). No update to counts. No mention of AI on the attacker side (2026-11-19, https://raiden.site.ktaiwork.jp/archives/4597 )

rows.organisation: Sanko Techno (internal servers of Vietnamese subsidiary SANKO FASTEM (VIETNAM))
rows.scale: 898 people (subsidiary-related persons) plus 10 officers/employees of the company and group companies; 1,348 Vietnamese business partners (companies)
rows.data: Individuals "(name, address, phone number, email address, identity documents, etc.)" / business partners "(company name, address, phone number, etc.)"
rows.dates: "In August 2026, in the subsidiary's information system" (no specific date stated). First notice (28 August): "We confirmed that [it] was subjected to unauthorised access by a third party (ransomware attack) and that some servers were encrypted."
rows.notes: Title "Notice regarding the occurrence of ransomware damage at an overseas consolidated subsidiary (final report)" (10 November 2026, timely disclosure; the same text as the tdnet original https://www.release.tdnet.info/inbs/140120261110571505.pdf confirmed on jpx). Wording of the vector: "unauthorised access by a third party occurred through a deficiency in the settings of network equipment" (admitted because it is not a case in which data was merely viewable due to a setting error but one involving intrusion, encryption and outflow by a third party). The first notice is "Notice regarding the occurrence of ransomware damage at an overseas consolidated subsidiary" (28 August 2026, https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/34350/140120260828527717.pdf ), with no mention of a leak or its possibility. Because the leak was first announced on 10 November, published was set to 2026-11-10 (the first-notice date of 28 August is outside the collection period; the handling needs a decision at merging). The aggregator site's "908 persons" is the sum of 898 persons and 10 persons.

Wording: "the direct cause is that the system's service account key leaked externally and was misused by a third party." (classified as unauthorised login). Many virtual servers were created and used for crypto mining. Follow-up "Notice of investigation results ..." (2026/11/10, https://progate.com/about/news/622) corrected the affected persons (employees plus event participants) and continues to treat it as a risk of leakage. The follow-up's description of an internal prototype tool where AI gives feedback describes the organisation's own system, not attacker AI. The company's other case is this file's 2026-11-17 row (Notion). WebFetch could not read the body (title metadata only); the body text was retrieved in a browser (Claude in Chrome) and checked. Moved from pending (21 November 2026). Missed in the additions through the 6th edition.

The first notice was "Report on unauthorised access to our service" of 13 November 2026 (https://plaid.co.jp/news/20261113/ ), which said "Because we detected unauthorised access by a third party to 'KARTE', we have suspended the entire KARTE service as emergency maintenance." and did not mention personal information, so published is set to 16 November, the first notice to state a leak of personal information (author's decision). (Follow-up of 20 November 2026) "Notice of our investigation results regarding unauthorised access to 'KARTE' and the outlook for resuming service" (https://plaid.co.jp/news/20261120/ ): vector "a vulnerability in part of the internal processing of a public path ultimately used to obtain data was exploited." "Unauthorised access to the KARTE admin console occurred using the obtained authentication information." Number of companies for information entrusted by companies: "part of the data integrated into KARTE" 570 companies, "part of end users' analytics data" 487, "part of end users' cache data" 409, "part of the authentication information used for integration with external services" 754 (the company counts pair the table's numbers with item names; the table rows' exact wording is unverified). Information held for the company's own purposes: "79,249 records" (email addresses for registration/login) and "information of people who gave us contact details in our sales activities and activities supporting use of our service (name, email address, etc.)" "45,816 records". Cache data: "we treat all data that may have been stored in the cache during the relevant time period as information that may have leaked." Correction to the 16 November wording: "We apologise for the incorrect expression and correct it." (information of companies that no longer have a KARTE contract was also included). Resumption target: "We have decided to set the target for the phased resumption of KARTE at mid-January 2027." Chain: KARTE (PLAID) origin row. Rows for KARTE client companies are handled by agents B to F2.

rows.organisation: Nulab (operating environment of the online whiteboard tool "Cacoo"; inquiry records)
rows.scale: approx. 792 records (subject to change). 2nd notice (18 November 2026): 765 inquiry records (confirmed), 890 billing records, 310 past internal survey records (not verified verbatim)
rows.data: "The records that flowed out include personal information such as the names, email addresses, phone numbers and addresses of customers who made inquiries, and some include the last four digits of credit card numbers etc."
rows.dates: "On the morning of 14 November 2026, we detected that an external third party was using our authentication information without authorisation in Cacoo's operating environment." Blocking: "We sequentially invalidated the authentication information and blocked access from the attack source." (no date)
rows.notes: Title "On the occurrence of unauthorised access in our service 'Cacoo' (1st notice)" (16 November 2026, Nulab Inc.; also disclosed via TDnet the same day, release.tdnet.info not retrieved). Wording of the vector is as in the dates field (classified as unauthorised login because of the misuse of authentication information; author's decision). "We have reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission." (added 16:00, 16 November 2026). Follow-up: 2nd notice "On the current status of the unauthorised access in our service 'Cacoo' (2nd notice)" (18 November 2026; same text as TDnet confirmed on minkabu: https://assets.minkabu.jp/news/article_media_content/urn:newsml:tdnet.info:20261118582953/140120261118582953.pdf) states "our authentication information was obtained through a mechanism related to Cacoo's video call function"; outflow of 765 inquiry records confirmed, and 890 billing records of PayPal users and 310 past internal survey records at risk of outflow (numbers and categories not verified verbatim). (Corrected 21 November 2026) 2nd report "Current status of the unauthorised access to our service 'Cacoo' (2nd report)" (same text as TDnet). "The number of personal information records contained in the leaked inquiry records, announced in the 1st report as 'approx. 792 (under review)', has been finalised at 765." "Main items: name, email address, phone number, address etc. Some include the last 4 digits of credit card information etc." Newly possible leak: billing information of an external payment service ("Main items: name, email address, phone number, transaction details (amount, contract plan name etc.)" "We confirmed that the authentication information for linking with the payment service may have been obtained by a third party." "As of now, it has not been confirmed that billing information was viewed."; 890 records, wording unverified), and past internal investigation data ("Main items: name, email address (includes authentication information for some customers ...)" "The data may have been obtained, and we are investigating."; 310 records, wording unverified). Route: "It was found that our authentication information was obtained through a mechanism related to Cacoo's video call function and used for unauthorised access to the operating environment." Detected on the morning of 14 November 2026 (wording unverified). A 3rd report followed on 20 November ("Prospects for resuming 'Cacoo' and current status of the unauthorised access (3rd report)"; body not read). (2026-11-18, https://assets.minkabu.jp/news/article_media_content/urn:newsml:tdnet.info:20261118582953/140120261118582953.pdf ) (Added 21 November 2026) 3rd report "Prospects for resuming our service 'Cacoo' and current status regarding unauthorised access (3rd report)" (TDnet 15:45). Inquiry records "[outflow confirmed]" 765 (main items "name, email address, phone number, address, etc.", "some include the last 4 digits of credit card information, etc."); billing information of an external payment service "[risk of outflow]" 890; part of past internal survey data "[risk of outflow]" 310 (numbers summarised; wording unverified). "Prospect for resumption: next week (24-27 November 2026)". No specific description of cause or route. The 2nd report was a timely disclosure at 18:00 on 18 November 2026. (2026-11-20, https://assets.minkabu.jp/news/article_media_content/urn:newsml:tdnet.info:20261120584334/140120261120584334.pdf )

rows.dates: Suspicious messages reported "from around late night on Monday 21 September 2026" (1st notice). Suspended "around 10:58 am on 24 September 2026", resumed "around 9:48 pm on 24 September 2026" (9 October 2026). Final report: "An attempted external access was observed on 26 August of the same year, but we confirmed that the intrusion by unauthorised access occurred on 21 September of the same year." "On 20 November 2026, we completed submission of the final report to the Personal Information Protection Commission based on the investigation results."
rows.notes: Title "Apology and notice regarding suspicious messages and unauthorised access to the company's system" (28 September 2026, Temairazu, Inc.). Basis for the judgement: "We confirmed that there was unauthorised access to the company's system." Suspicious messages were sent "via messaging apps such as WhatsApp, email, SMS, etc." On the vector, the 1st notice says "We refrain from disclosing the specific method of the unauthorised access and the details of the measures taken", and the final report says "We confirmed that a third party misused some functions of the application to carry out unauthorised access." "We refrain from disclosing technical details such as the specific intrusion route and attack method."; hence classified as unauthorised access (vector not disclosed) (whether 'misused some functions' counts as a vulnerability is for the author to decide). Follow-ups: 7 October 2026 "Investigation status and future response regarding unauthorised access (2nd report)" (wording unverified); 9 October 2026 timely disclosure "Investigation status and response regarding unauthorised access to the company's system" (https://assets.minkabu.jp/news/article_media_content/urn:newsml:tdnet.info:20261009548929/140120261009548929.pdf , "up to approx. 4.45 million persons"); 20 November 2026 "Report on the investigation results regarding unauthorised access to the company's system (final report)" (https://www.temairazu.co.jp/pdf/1220/news-update , revised to up to approx. 1 million; no reason for the revision stated). The company's separate incident (2026-11-09, via Arara) is a separate row. Notices by accommodation facilities were not searched. Missed in the additions up to the 6th edition (found by tracing the final report in the timely disclosures back to the 1st notice). (Added 21 November 2026) The first notice (28 September 2026) was rechecked: "For security reasons, we refrain from disclosing the specific method of the unauthorised access and the details of the measures taken." The vector stays "unauthorised access (route not disclosed)"; the final report's "misuse of some functions of the application" is kept in the notes as a description of the method.

rows.organisation: SBC Medical Group Holdings (database held by SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd. on behalf of partner medical institutions; external booking service "Tribeau" used by group medical institutions)
rows.scale: "The number of customers concerned is 1,030,349 persons for item 1, 881 persons for item 2, 6,155 persons for item 3, 28,617 persons for item 4 and 19,464 persons for item 5." Part of credit card information: "14 persons concerned" (contents of items 1-5 are in an image table, not verified; no overall total in the text)
rows.status: Confirmed leak ("damage occurred in which customers' personal information was illegally obtained")
rows.data: "We have confirmed that customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, dates of birth, passwords, member IDs, booking application details via specific web booking forms, and content entered via web inquiry forms, etc. were illegally obtained." Group staff account information and part of credit card information in inquiry forms (wording not verified). Not affected: "At present, it has not been confirmed that electronic medical records (records of treatment) of the group's medical institutions were illegally obtained."
rows.dates: "On 16 November 2026 (Mon), SBC confirmed unauthorised access to the database concerned, immediately isolated the server concerned from the network and blocked the unauthorised access." Start of intrusion not stated
rows.notes: Title "Apology and notice regarding the outflow of personal information due to unauthorised access damage to SBC Medical Group (1st notice)" (19 November 2026 11:30, SBC Medical Group Holdings Inc.). Wording of the vector: "It was caused by a third party carrying out continuous attacks, 770,000 times from overseas, on the system concerned during late-night hours." Intrusion method under investigation (wording not verified). Also: "In addition, we confirmed, through a report from the operator of the service, that the personal information of customers who made bookings was also illegally obtained in the external booking service 'Tribeau' used by the group's medical institutions." (Tribeau side: unauthorised logins; affected "55 Shonan Beauty Clinic branches, Ritz Cosmetic Surgery Tokyo"). Classified as composite because of two routes: an attack on the company's own database and unauthorised logins to an external booking service (author's decision). Tribeau's own notice is in a separate row. The notice is outside the organisation's own domain (PR TIMES); sbc-holdings.com/ja/news/605 could not be opened with WebFetch. Moved from pending "SBC Medical Group Holdings (unauthorised access to SBC Medical Group)". The company is a NASDAQ-listed holding company in the US but its business is support for medical institutions in Japan (admitted as Japan-based). (Added 21 November 2026) On admission criterion 5: the sender is a Nasdaq-listed holding company in the United States, but the incident occurred in the systems of its Japanese subsidiary, SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd., and in a booking service used by clinics in Japan. It is admitted as an incident at a Japanese place of business (author's decision).
